Authorities in the Philippines took an Indonesian citizen into custody on Wednesday, identifying him as a suspected militant involved in the takeover of portions of Marawi back in May. Law enforcement and military authorities confirmed the operation. The occupation had previously sparked widespread anxiety that the area was transforming into a base for the Islamic State across Southeast Asia, which in turn prompted a grueling five-month campaign by the armed forces to dislodge the insurgents, a mix of local rebels and foreign fighters from places like Malaysia, Indonesia, and the Middle East.

According to Colonel Romeo Brawner, who serves as the deputy commander for the Marawi task force, local peacekeepers apprehended the suspect early Wednesday morning. Zia Alonto Adiong, a local official aiding relief and rescue efforts, remarked in an official statement that the capture underscores how crucial civilian involvement is for safeguarding neighborhoods from extremist threats. 

The apprehension occurred just a day after security forces fatally shot another pro-Islamic State fighter, and roughly a week and a half after the conclusion of the military campaign in the Philippines. The months-long siege resulted in a death toll exceeding 1,100—primarily militants—and forced roughly 350,000 residents to flee their homes.

Lanao del Sur provincial police chief John Guyguyon stated that the detained individual gave his name as Muhammad Ilham Shaputra, a 23-year-old hailing from Medan City in North Sumatra. Guyguyon explained that the suspect was intercepted while attempting to flee across a lake. Inside his bag, authorities discovered a mobile phone, a .45-caliber pistol, a hand grenade, Philippine and Indonesian money, and Saudi riyals.

Law enforcement intends to prosecute the suspect for his involvement in the early stages of the siege, as Guyguyon noted during a press briefing, mentioning that investigators are currently assembling the paperwork to charge him with rebellion, terrorism-related offenses, and additional counts. Furthermore, Guyguyon revealed that the captive admitted that several other armed individuals are still remaining in concealment within the primary combat zone of central Marawi. 

Investigators also established that Shaputra traveled to the Philippines late last year, having been brought in by Isnilon Hapilon, who acted as the leader of the Islamic State in Southeast Asia and was slain in Marawi the previous month. 

While thousands of displaced citizens have begun making their way back, certain returnees have discovered their properties looted. Meanwhile, the central combat zone continues to be restricted to the public until teams can thoroughly inspect and clear the area of potential booby traps and unexploded military ordnance.

Donald Trump Humiliates Himself With Panama Leader; Panama And Twitter Humiliate Trump (VIDEO)

True to his usual form, Donald Trump apparently skipped any kind of preparation prior to welcoming Panamanian President Juan Carlos Varela into the Oval Office. Attempting to establish some common ground during the initial photo opportunity, Trump seemed to claim personal credit for the construction of the Panama Canal—a waterway completed roughly a century ago, with its eventual return to Panama having been arranged during the Carter administration. Neither Varela nor users on Twitter let the moment pass without comment.

The specific interaction was brief. Boasting in his typical manner, Trump stated, "It’s our great honor to have President and Mrs. Varela from Panama. We have many things to discuss. We’re going to spend quite a bit of time today. The Panama Canal is doing quite well, I think we did a good job building it." 

Varela replied with a concise four-word correction: "One hundred years ago."

Seemingly missing the remark, Trump continued, "We did a very good job. But things are going well in Panama. The relationship has been very strong. We are developing new things to do and only getting stronger. And our—also friendship with the President is very, very good." 

The canal was actually finished back in 1914, more than a century prior. Given that Trump is 71 years old, social media users pointed out that he likely would have covered the topic in elementary school. 

Reactions on Twitter came swiftly:

Panama Canal

#yourewelcome #panamacanal" — UnpresidentedAF ?? (@UnpresidentedAF) June 19, 2017

"Trump just took credit for building the Panama Canal. Now he’s pissed off the ghost of Teddy Roosevelt." — John Fugelsang (@JohnFugelsang) June 19, 2017

Other commentators questioned the assessment that the canal is performing well:

While the United States did indeed construct the Panama Canal, making Trump's statement technically correct in a broad sense, the moment highlights what critics viewed as a lack of intellectual effort. For comparison, remarks made by President Obama during his meeting with Varela two years prior tell a different story:

"Well, I just want to thank President Varela and the entire team, and the people of Panama, for the incredible hospitality. I had a chance earlier to visit the Panama Canal for the first time and saw the extraordinary progress that’s being made in the new development that will be completed next year. It’s really a symbol of human ingenuity, but also Panama’s central role in bridging the two continents and bringing the hemisphere together.

And I congratulated the President not only on what I’m certain will be a successful summit, but also the extraordinary progress that Panama has made economically, the transparency and accountability that his government has shown. Panama is a proud democracy, and its ability to engage in elections and peaceful transfers of power I think is a symbol of the progress that’s been made throughout the hemisphere over the last several decades.

And as President Varela noted, we are great partners on a whole range of issues—security, the economy, education—and we had an excellent discussion about how we can further deepen those ties."
Source: White House Archives

In short, Obama reviewed the background material and familiarized himself with the nation prior to meeting its head of state. Trump, conversely, appeared to hear the word "Panama" and immediately default to the only associated term that came to mind—canal—treating it as the sum total of what Panama represents.

South Africa's newly chosen African National Congress president, Cyril Ramaphosa, declared on Thursday that his priorities include eradicating graft and advancing a "radical economic transformation" strategy that accelerates the seizure of land without payment. Positioned to potentially take over as the nation's leader following the 2019 polls due to the political strength of the ANC, the 65-year-old—who transitioned from labor organizing to business and amassed substantial wealth—has received a warm welcome from international markets eager for his anti-corruption pledges and economic renewal agenda. 

Speaking in the early morning hours on Thursday following a protracted delay at the conclusion of a five-day gathering where he secured his position, Ramaphosa emphasized that tackling graft must be approached with the same vigor applied to joblessness, poverty, and social disparity. He added that the party must deal sternly with internal wrongdoings and misconduct. 

Having won the ANC leadership race on Monday as the successor to Jacob Zuma—whose tenure has been dogged by graft scandals—the current deputy president emerged from a tight contest against Nkosazana Dlamini-Zuma, a 68-year-old former cabinet minister and African Union Commission leader. This outcome marks a crucial turning point for the liberation movement that brought black-majority governance to the country 23 years ago under Nelson Mandela, though it currently faces severe internal rifts and a damaged reputation. 

During his address, Ramaphosa acknowledged Zuma, expressing a commitment to party unity despite the contentious race, noting that Zuma had previously supported his former spouse for the role. Nevertheless, financial markets remain anxious about Ramaphosa's capacity to implement reforms, given an evenly divided party leadership core—the "Top Six"—split equally between his supporters and those aligned with Dlamini-Zuma. Observers caution that having Ramaphosa lead the party while Zuma retains the national presidency could result in stalled decision-making or mixed signals. John Ashbourne, an economist at Capital Economics Africa, pointed out in a written commentary that Zuma's remaining tenure creates a dual-power dynamic likely to induce a phase of unclear policymaking. 

Anticipation of Ramaphosa's success initially drove the rand to 12.5200 against the dollar on Monday, marking its strongest level since late March when a presidential cabinet shakeup rattled markets and prompted credit downgrades to speculative grade. After dipping on Tuesday, the currency rebounded mid-week as markets continued evaluating his political leverage. Geoff Blount, managing director at BayHill Capital, characterized the outcome as a triumph for Ramaphosa that did not spell total defeat for Zuma. 

Zuma has consistently denied any culpability regarding corruption accusations levied against him since taking office in 2009, including claims that affluent Gupta associates exerted inappropriate control over the administration—allegations that both the president and the Gupta family have rejected. Without naming names, Ramaphosa touched upon these issues during his remarks, stating that the government must acknowledge how vital state institutions have been compromised by specific persons and relatives through undue sway and the distortion of public resources and governance. He noted that this dynamic has undermined state-run companies across the continent's most developed market, which has suffered from sluggish economic expansion over the past six years alongside near-record unemployment. 

Ramaphosa also issued a caution directed at business leaders, stating that authorities need to examine accounting scandals without bias, pointing to recent market volatility and massive investment losses for everyday citizens. This reference followed a recent crisis at South African furniture enterprise Steinhoff, which lost over $10 billion in market value over a fortnight due to an ongoing accounting investigation.

Furthermore, the newly minted ANC chief committed to fast-tracking employment generation, revitalizing the sluggish economy, and accelerating land redistribution to the black population. More than twenty years post-apartheid, the ruling party faces growing demands to correct racial imbalances in property ownership, where white citizens hold the vast majority of acreage. Ramaphosa stated that the gathering agreed that taking land without financial compensation ought to form part of the government's toolkit for reform and redistribution, noting these transfers will be fast-tracked under the broad radical economic transformation initiative aimed at addressing racial inequality.

SHANGHAI/BEIJING (Reuters) - State media outlets in China expressed optimism on Saturday regarding the encounter between U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping, viewing the summit as proof that a clash between the two global superpowers is not preordained. 

The official publication *China Daily* noted in an editorial that it was heartening to watch the two-day gathering conclude on Friday “going as well as it could,” particularly in light of prior mixed messages emanating from Washington concerning bilateral ties. Earlier, Trump had utilized sharp anti-China rhetoric during his campaign and provoked Beijing prior to his inauguration by speaking with the leader of Taiwan, a self-governing island claimed by China. Nevertheless, at the Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida, the participants steered clear of any diplomatic missteps that might have offended Beijing's strict adherence to protocol.

According to *China Daily*, both governments demonstrated a shared eagerness to foster a constructive partnership. The editorial remarked that this might seem unexpected to observers convinced of an unavoidable clash between an incumbent superpower and a rising nation, yet the success Washington and Beijing have achieved in averting disputes demonstrates that hostility is not mandatory.

Meanwhile, the state-backed tabloid *Global Times* characterized the summit as a sign that bilateral relations remained steady following the inauguration of the Trump administration in January, suggesting the superpowers are poised to forge a more practical dynamic. The publication added that both nations appear to recognize the necessity of a seamless transition, a priority that carries global significance.

These sentiments were reinforced by a front-page piece in the overseas edition of the Communist Party’s flagship newspaper, *People’s Daily*, which asserted that the summit set the overarching direction for future relations between the nations. 

On Saturday, Trump posted a message on Twitter describing the encounter, stating that mutual respect and camaraderie had been established, though the future of trade agreements remains to be seen. Notably, the commentaries published in Chinese media omitted any reference to the American missile attack on a Syrian military airfield, an event that occurred simultaneously with the summit.

Wang Dong, an associate professor specializing in international studies at Peking University, suggested that the strike may have appealed to Trump as a signal to North Korea regarding its nuclear ambitions, though he doubted Beijing would be overly rattled. Wang pointed out the vast distinctions between the conflicts in Syria and the Korean Peninsula, highlighting Pyongyang's conventional military capacity to retaliate against South Korea should Washington take military action. Any pre-emptive strikes or use of force against North Korea would entail massive consequences, producing results vastly different from the situation in Syria, Wang explained.

During the negotiations, Trump urged Xi to exert greater pressure on North Korea to rein in its nuclear program. Additionally, the leaders established a 100-day framework for commercial negotiations designed to expand American exports and shrink the substantial trade deficit the United States runs with Beijing. 

American commercial sectors had anticipated that Trump would firmly press Xi behind closed doors to dismantle trade practices deemed discriminatory, while avoiding reckless moves that might trigger a trade conflict. In a development likely to be well-received domestically, the official Xinhua news agency reported that representatives from both countries launched fresh negotiation frameworks covering economic, diplomatic, and security matters. This initiative appeared to reshape the conventional Strategic and Economic Dialogue format utilized during the administration of former President Barack Obama.

Certain figures within American business circles had previously criticized those legacy talks for producing minimal tangible progress, advising the Trump administration to abandon them until Beijing demonstrated greater willingness to resolve grievances regarding industrial regulations. Jacob Parker, who serves as vice president of China operations for the U.S.-China Business Council in Beijing, noted a preference for concrete, results-driven achievements from these newly established talks rather than extensive, unfocused agendas, while still describing the summit as largely favorable for business interests.

PUBLIX Grocery Chain Directs All Stores To BLOCK National Enquirer Magazines With Trump On Cover [VIDEO]

The Florida-based supermarket company Publix has instructed all of its retail locations to conceal the front of the National Enquirer using white plastic shields, following a month-long run of issues highlighting President-elect Donald Trump. This decision by the company came in response to feedback from shoppers. Images captured at a Publix in Central Florida on December 28 document the concealment of the National Enquirer issue displaying the Trump family. At this store, the Enquirer was positioned alongside other tabloid publications that lacked any censorship screens over their front pages. 

Issues of the Enquirer bearing Donald Trump's photograph and name on the cover included publication dates of November 28, December 5, December 12, December 19, and December 26 in the year 2016, alongside the January 2, 2017 edition featuring the Trump family. Typically, the listed publication dates precede the actual retail release by roughly a week and a half. 

WFTX-TV initially broke the story regarding the actions taken by Publix on December 21, acting on a tip provided by an upset supporter of Trump. 

Watch here:

A customer shopping at Publix contacted Four in Your Corner after discovering that publications featuring the picture of President-elect Donald Trump were being obscured inside the store. His visit took place at the Publix located at the intersection of Del Prado Boulevard and Kismet Parkway situated in Cape Coral. 

Shopper Walter Indyk stated, "I lift it up and there was a picture of Donald Trump, the President-elect. I was like 'Wow, really? I mean, what's next?'" 

"The white screen covers are usually for magazines with inappropriate language or pictures. I was flabbergasted. I was amazed. I couldn't believe it," Indyk continued. "I was like 'This guy's going to be the President. They have the nerve to cover his picture up at the check out aisle?'"

Another Cape Coral resident, Rachael McDonnell, remarked, "I don't understand what is trying to be protected here. Whether everybody likes it or not, Trump is the President-elect."

According to Indyk, when he spoke with the store manager, he was informed that the location had received numerous complaints regarding the magazine's presence, and that the directive came from corporate headquarters. 

Inquiries were made by Four in Your Corner to the corporate office of Publix. A representative provided a statement which read, in part: "The National Enquirer receives the most customer complaints about front page content, so they were added to the list of magazines required to be covered, just last week." 

For decades, the National Enquirer had been available in Publix checkout lanes without being hidden, up until the period following Trump's election victory on November 8, after which he appeared on the cover week following week. 

Kristinn Taylor, writing for The Gateway Pundit as their Florida representative, spoke with a Publix manager who confirmed that the controversy stemmed from incoming complaint calls. The White House has unveiled its specifications for Trump's proposed border wall, which the president continues to promote as the ultimate fix for all issues. Alongside the federal government issuing "notices of taking" to property owners in Texas situated along the U.S.-Mexico border, the administration's official requirements have now been made public. Fox News shared the list on Twitter, and the contents are remarkably absurd. Border wall requirements. pic.twitter.com/AFYG0s5pCS Fox News (@FoxNews) March 19, 2017

At an initial glance, the post might seem like a prank, but the verified blue checkmark on the Fox News Twitter account confirms its authenticity. The humor in these three requirements stems from their extreme vagueness, effectively rendering them completely devoid of substance. It feels as though Fox contacted Trump unexpectedly to ask for the specifications of the barrier, and he responded on the spot with vague affirmations. The list lacks any updated cost projections, details on material placement, strategies to prevent disruption to wildlife migration, plans for managing diverted floodwaters, or any details that would genuinely outline the project's technical demands. Instead, it features three ambiguous points that suggest the administration prioritizes promoting the wall over realistic logistical planning.

The final two points on the list are particularly peculiar: the structure must "look good from U.S. side" and simultaneously appear "imposing" from the Mexican side. Aside from bearing a resemblance to something a child might write, it is clear that residents do not want an unsightly barrier in their immediate vicinity. Yet, a thirty-foot wall risks being an eyesore regardless of aesthetic efforts to soften its appearance. Residents living near the Rio Grande, whose current views consist of the river and who share close ties with neighboring communities in Mexico, stand to face negative impacts from a towering wall. There are no plans to construct it out of Plexiglas to preserve scenery; rather, it is mandated to project an "imposing" presence to observers on the other side. 

In practice, while certain areas might see an increase in property values, others could experience severe economic downturns if visitors from neighboring towns are no longer able to cross over to shop. Aesthetic considerations will provide little comfort to the communities facing negative consequences. Another requirement states the structure must be "difficult to climb or cut through." This is hardly a revelation, given that the administration has consistently maintained that preventing individuals from scaling or breaching the barrier—unlike existing fencing—is the primary purpose of the project. Even so, individuals will likely attempt to climb it, dig underneath it, or bypass it entirely through the oceans. 

When factoring in that the majority of undocumented immigrants arrive in the United States legally using visitor visas and simply overstay them, the demand for a wall that is "difficult to climb or cut through" becomes even more ridiculous. Taxpayers funding the project deserve a clear understanding of what the administration believes the wall will actually entail across all operational aspects. Ultimately, many would prefer the administration abandon the concept entirely, viewing the allocation of taxpayer dollars as a massive misdirection of time, money, and resources. Featured image by Chip Somodevilla via Getty Images

Consider Justice Ginsburg officiating at a gay marriage ceremony—did anyone genuinely anticipate an objective ruling from her on the matter? Last week provided a striking illustration of why implementing term limits for Supreme Court justices deserves serious consideration. Anyone suggesting those rulings lacked political motivation is simply fooling themselves. The current Supreme Court has abandoned both the Constitution and the rule of law in favor of a fundamental transformation. Andrew McCarthy offers a brilliant perspective on the recent actions of the high court:

This tribunal functions as anything but a legislature. Chief Justice John Roberts explicitly included that exact sentiment within his dissenting opinion on same-sex marriage released Friday. This came merely twenty-four hours following the performance by his colleague in the legislative overhaul of the Affordable Care Act—previously known as Obamacare, though now permanently dubbed SCOTUScare courtesy of the scathing dissent penned by Justice Antonin Scalia.

The denial by Roberts that the judicial branch acts legislatively is remarkably cynical. By rescuing SCOTUScare, the chief justice enthusiastically seized the law-making authority of Congress. He first assumed the power to divine legislative intent from contradictory statutory wording, and subsequently manufactured legislative ambiguity to justify twisting the text toward a predetermined outcome. Pulling off such a maneuver one day while denouncing the very concept the next requires an extraordinary level of shamelessness.

A massive volume of commentary has already been produced to examine, praise, and criticize the court's actions this week. These included a second lifeline thrown to SCOTUScare within a mere three-year span, the sudden discovery of a previously unknown constitutional right to same-sex marriage nearly a century and a half after the Fourteenth Amendment was ratified, and the reshaping of the Fair Housing Act passed by Congress to incorporate the peculiar disparate-impact theory of discrimination favored by legal academia.

Despite this relentless stream of analysis, a crucial detail remains almost entirely ignored—the very omission that best illuminates this week's trifecta of fundamental transformation. 

Was there even a shred of uncertainty regarding how the four progressive justices would cast their votes? Not a single person doubted their path. Across the vast collection of opinions produced in these three cases, neither Ruth Bader Ginsburg, Stephen Breyer, Elena Kagan, nor Sonia Sotomayor authored even one. There was simply no necessity for it. They operate as the designated voting bloc of the political left. The sun had a higher probability of failing to rise than any of them breaking ranks.

How is such uniformity possible? Legal interpretation is inherently complex. Flexible intellects, regardless of shared perspectives, frequently diverge—sometimes dramatically—over principles of constitutional review, methods of statutory interpretation, murky boundaries of the separation of powers, the nuances of language, and numerous other factors. One need only look to the vigorous disagreement between the court's two originalist members, Scalia and Clarence Thomas, regarding a statute treating Jerusalem as sovereign Israeli territory in direct opposition to administration policy.

Yet such variation never appears among the court's leftist bloc, particularly regarding major cases.

This phenomenon goes beyond merely moving in lockstep; the true issue is that nobody expects them to act otherwise. Their fellow justices, members of the political branches, and commentators from across the political spectrum share this expectation.

It is now universally accepted that these justices are not present to adjudicate. They are there strictly to cast ballots. They reach predetermined conclusions using the same backward logic employed by disparate-impact theories to manufacture discrimination—starting at the finish line and working backward. Established precedents are relegated to the quaint traditions of administering actual justice. Within the realm of social justice, entirely unprecedented paths are embraced when familiar ones fail to lead where desired.

A fundamental problem arises here. Once it becomes an accepted reality that a vital faction of the Supreme Court is no longer expected—let alone required—to practice law, the tribunal ceases to function as a legal entity, transforming instead into a purely political body.

That represents our current reality. We should abandon the pretense that this court deserves the safeguards our system established for a non-political branch, such as lifetime appointments, insulation from elections, and the veil of secrecy protecting judicial deliberations.

If these justices intend to engage in politics, they belong within the realm of electoral politics. If John Roberts insists on writing laws while simultaneously pretending he lacks the power to do so, or if Anthony Kennedy genuinely believes the nation desires his eccentric interpretation of liberty—condemning government restrictions on marriage just a day after tightening government control over a significant portion of the American economy—then their seats do not belong in an isolated third branch of government. They belong inside an accountable third chamber of Congress.

If society wishes to retain some harmless relic of this charade for old times' sake, the justices may continue wearing their judicial robes to the office—at least for as long as they can convince voters to keep them employed. Regardless, we must discard the fiction that their legal rulings stem from genuine jurisprudence rather than sheer political will.

Tetzner abandoned the sect, which is led by convicted rapist Warren Jeffs, eight years ago, and she successfully secured full custody of her kids just last week.

However, upon arriving in the Colorado City, Utah, community to collect them, she encountered physical resistance from a massive crowd of sect members determined to retain the children. Flora Jessop, a former cult member who assisted Tetzner during the legal proceedings, recounted to KSL that community members flooded the area, swarming the home, yard, fences, and vehicle, kicking the van, and even attempting to place a cow and chickens inside the automobile. 

Mobile phone recordings depict crowds of polygamists encircling the van, with female members wearing traditional pastel-colored, floor-length dresses. Although a Mohave County judge mandated that the sect surrender the minors by 5:00 p.m. Thursday, Tetzner reported that the children were absent when she arrived at the designated time. 

The kids did not reappear until midnight, at which point they were immediately ushered into the residence of their aunt, Samantha Holm, where dozens of fundamentalists blocked the mother from seeing them. Tetzner remained in her van overnight, worried that abandoning the vehicle would result in it being dismantled. By morning, approximately 600 cult members had surrounded the vehicle and blocked her path to the house where the children were housed, prompting Tetzner to contact law enforcement for assistance. 

Sheriff's deputies were forced to secure a search warrant in order to remove the children from the house and place them into their mother's custody. Reports indicate the children were reluctant to depart because cult members had frightened them with claims that their mother was leading them to hell. Deputies accompanied Tetzner and the children all the way back to their northern Utah residence, while FLDS members reportedly followed them the entire journey.

The non-profit organization Defenders of Children, which has supported Tetzner throughout the custody dispute, expressed concern for her safety and initiated fundraising efforts to cover the costs of a security system and fresh clothing for the children. Legislation passed by the U.S. House of Representatives on Thursday includes a $68 billion boost to defense spending for the upcoming year, alongside funding to kick off construction on the Mexican border wall championed by President Donald Trump. Growing worries over North Korea—which successfully tested an intercontinental ballistic missile in July and is developing a greater capacity to strike the U.S. with nuclear weapons—prompted the legislative increase aimed at bolstering foreign missile defense capabilities. While the measure allocates $1.6 billion to begin building the southern border barrier promised during Trump’s 2016 campaign, that amount is heavily overshadowed by the broader $658.1 billion earmarked for the Defense Department. This defense figure sits $68.1 billion higher than the fiscal year 2017 enacted levels and exceeds Trump’s own budget request by $18.4 billion.

Passing by a 235-192 margin, the fiscal 2018 spending legislation faced fierce opposition from Democrats, who have consistently labeled any wall funding as a "poison pill" and are expected to fight to strip it out in the Senate. Lawmakers are racing toward an October 1 deadline, which marks the beginning of the new fiscal year, requiring them to either pass spending legislation or enact temporary funding extensions at current levels to buy negotiators more time. Republican leadership slipped the border wall money into the expansive national security appropriations bill at the eleventh hour, gambling that representatives opposed to the wall would still vote "yes" rather than torpedo the entire defense package. 

Throughout his campaign and presidency, Trump has insisted on the necessity of a large wall spanning the entirety of the southwestern border, maintaining that Mexico would eventually foot the bill. However, Mexico has adamantly refused to pay, and Trump recently conceded that certain stretches of the border might not be suitable for a barrier. Both Democratic lawmakers and numerous Republicans have raised doubts regarding the practicality and efficacy of the project, while immigration advocates contend it would fail to stop unauthorized crossings and would strain diplomatic ties between the U.S. and Mexico. 

Recent interviews with more than six Republican senators from states that backed Trump in November revealed that only Ted Cruz of Texas fully supported the wall's construction. In a similar vein, House Republicans whose districts border Mexico have spoken out against the barrier, the total cost of which could ultimately surpass $21 billion. Representative Nita Lowey, the top Democrat on the House Appropriations Committee, dismissed the wall as an unnecessary and ineffective waste that contradicts American values. Lowey also pointed out that the Pentagon's proposed funding creates a legal hurdle by exceeding current defense spending caps by $72 billion. She warned that enacting the bill into law would automatically trigger a 13 percent across-the-board cut to every single defense account to comply with the statutory limits.

Even with these hurdles, the expanded defense budget enables the Pentagon to sustain ongoing operations in Afghanistan, Iraq, and other conflict zones, recruit additional service members, and grant troops a 2.4 percent salary increase. It additionally funds a major purchasing push for heavy military equipment, providing resources for new tanks, aircraft, ships, and submarines. 

Additional provisions in the House-approved measure allocate more money for the Department of Energy to manage the U.S. nuclear weapons stockpile. Increased funding is also directed to the U.S. Capitol Police following the June 14 shooting that left Republican Representative Steve Scalise seriously injured. 

The Missile Defense Agency is slated to receive an $825 million increase, pushing its total budget past $8.6 billion—surpassing the president's request. This includes funding for extra silos and boosters for the primary system designed to counter ICBM threats, a project overseen by Boeing Co., alongside 14 additional THAAD interceptors produced by Lockheed Martin Co.

WASHINGTON (Reuters) - Speaking before senators on Wednesday, billionaire investor and U.S. President-elect Donald Trump’s nominee for commerce secretary, Wilbur Ross, leveled heavy criticism against Beijing’s trade habits, promising to find fresh strategies to counter them during his confirmation hearing. Ross further indicated that the incoming administration would likely place the renegotiation of the North American Free Trade Agreement involving Canada and Mexico at the very top of its agenda, describing the task as an extremely early priority. Having built his wealth by revitalizing struggling businesses across sectors like textiles, automotive components, and steel, the 79-year-old nominee characterized China as the biggest protectionist major economy, pointing to its extensive tariff and non-tariff import barriers. 

Ross committed to establishing a fair environment for American enterprises facing Chinese competition or attempting to operate within China, remarking that Chinese officials preach free trade far more than they execute it. The goal, he explained, is to match those realities with the rhetoric. These remarks followed an address in Davos, Switzerland, where Chinese President Xi Jinping championed free trade, advocated for a broader international leadership position for Beijing, and termed the nation's economy wide open. Responding during a regular briefing in Beijing on Thursday, Chinese foreign ministry spokeswoman Hua Chunying questioned who was genuinely advancing trade and investment liberalization versus who was practicing protectionism, asserting that the reality differs entirely from Ross’s assessment.

According to Ross, Chinese state-owned enterprises represent a distinct issue requiring attention, as roughly a third of them persistently operate without profit, generating an overcapacity that results in the dumping of commodities such as aluminum and steel. Calling state-backed bank funding an artificial subsidy, he warned that the Commerce Department would rigorously track down unfair subsidies necessitating countervailing duties. While he avoided explicit references to Trump's warnings regarding punitive tariffs on Chinese imports, Ross maintained that nations engaging in below-cost product dumping or failing to maintain fair trade conditions ought to face severe punishment, highlighting steel and aluminum as areas requiring particular focus for anti-dumping tariffs. Furthermore, he mentioned that the Commerce Department might independently launch anti-dumping and anti-subsidy investigations to speed up proceedings, bypassing the need for private companies to assemble the cases. Ross also expressed concern over Chinese acquisitions of American entertainment and distribution companies, contrasting it with Beijing's restrictions blocking U.S. firms from similar opportunities inside China.

Both China’s trade approaches and NAFTA have faced frequent attacks from Trump, who blames them for the disappearance of millions of manufacturing jobs in America. The president-elect has vowed to either overhaul the 23-year-old accord to better serve domestic manufacturers or withdraw from it altogether. Citing a report by the Toronto Globe and Mail on Wednesday, Canadian officials were reportedly told by Ross that a formal negotiation request would be delivered shortly after the presidential inauguration on Friday, with rules of origin serving as a key focus. 

Turning to broader economic prospects, Ross expressed confidence that the U.S. economy could outperform the Obama administration's growth rate, suggesting that reaching approximately 3 percent growth is feasible through the implementation of Trump's agenda. This plan includes scaling back regulatory burdens on businesses, boosting domestic energy output, narrowing trade deficits, and repairing deteriorating national infrastructure. Additionally, Ross emphasized the private sector's need for increased wireless telecommunications spectrum—sales of which fall under the Commerce Department's purview—and promised to lobby government and military entities holding the spectrum to relinquish unused portions. 

Clarifying his overall stance, Ross stated that he is not anti-trade, but rather pro-sensible trade that avoids harming American workers and the manufacturing sector. To prevent conflicts of interest should he assume the commerce secretary role—a job encompassing duties from trade enforcement and economic data releases to weather forecasting and telecommunications auctions—Ross revealed on Tuesday that he plans to divest up to roughly $300 million in investments, which includes his ownership interest in his private equity firm.

WASHINGTON — House Republicans are mounting an effort to pursue contempt of Congress charges against Consumer Financial Protection Bureau Director Richard Cordray, accusing him of failing to adequately answer congressional subpoenas. According to a document published Friday by GOP staff members on the House Financial Services Committee, sufficient grounds exist to hold Cordray accountable for his alleged non-compliance. Committee Republicans have consistently targeted the consumer watchdog's regulatory agenda with sharp criticism. 

This latest report represents the most aggressive move yet toward potential legal measures against Cordray, an appointee of former Democratic President Barack Obama. The agency he leads was established under the 2010 Dodd-Frank financial reform legislation. 

At the center of the subpoena dispute are records related to the agency's push to prohibit mandatory arbitration clauses in financial agreements—a move that successfully concluded in July and drew praise from consumer advocates, even as congressional Republicans seek to reverse it. The requested documents were part of an investigation into the rulemaking process to determine if the regulations surrounding these clauses were developed appropriately. Such mandatory clauses typically force consumers into arbitration for dispute resolution, blocking them from participating in class-action lawsuits. 

Although GOP staff on the banking panel initially floated the possibility of contempt proceedings back in June over what they deemed inadequate replies, Friday's document escalates the dispute significantly. Jeff Emerson, a spokesperson for the committee, did not immediately reply to inquiries regarding whether the panel intends to formally pursue the charges. 

Meanwhile, CFPB representative Jen Howard defended the bureau's cooperation, noting in a statement to Reuters that the agency has already handed over thousands of pages of materials and is working to supply more. She emphasized that the bureau remains committed to figuring out how to address the committee's demands satisfactorily. Cordray himself has previously pushed back against the panel's document requests, describing them in the past as excessively broad and unclear. 

Representative Jeb Hensarling, who leads the committee, remains one of Cordray's most vocal adversaries and previously urged Republican President Donald Trump to dismiss the director. Conversely, Democrats have offered steadfast support to both the bureau and its head since the agency's inception. Maxine Waters, the senior Democrat on Hensarling's committee, dismissed the Republican push in a statement to Reuters, calling the attacks on the agency and its director completely groundless and asserting there is no justification for a contempt citation.

LIMA (Reuters) — The Brazilian construction conglomerate Odebrecht announced on Saturday that the newly revealed commercial connections involving embattled Peruvian leader Pedro Pablo Kuczynski were entirely separate from the illicit agreements it has already confessed to investigators. This statement could potentially bolster Kuczynski’s efforts to fend off an upcoming removal vote scheduled for Thursday in the opposition-controlled Congress, where lawmakers are accusing him of accepting bribes from the firm at the center of the region's largest corruption probe.

Earlier in the week, in response to a formal request from Congress, Odebrecht provided a document outlining $4.8 million in payments made to a pair of firms belonging to Kuczynski or a close associate for financial and advisory consulting. While Kuczynski had previously disavowed any association with the company, he has refused to step down over the payments, maintaining that the transactions were entirely legal and above board.

Odebrecht also pushed back against claims from a prominent journalist at the *La Republica* newspaper suggesting that the release of the information was part of a coordinated plot with the conservative opposition to oust Kuczynski. The company explained that it was permitted to share the details regarding these specific transactions because there was no indication they were connected to its past criminal conduct, matters it is strictly restricted to discussing solely with public prosecutors.

In a letter addressed to *La Republica* and shared publicly via Twitter on Saturday, Odebrecht stated that the funds were properly compensated and fully accounted for in official records. The firm emphasized that it has a legal duty to provide requested documentation to appropriate government bodies, which includes the congressional investigative panel. 

Odebrecht sent shockwaves through the political landscape across Latin America a year ago when it publicly admitted to running complex bribery networks spanning over ten countries for more than ten years, resulting in the imprisonment of prominent figures from Colombia to the Dominican Republic. 

Late Friday, members of Congress secured the necessary votes to initiate proceedings to declare the presidency vacant, setting up Thursday's vote that could remove Kuczynski from office. Allies of the center-right leader pointed to the company's letter to argue that his sole mistake was having given misleading statements regarding his past ties to the builder. Should Congress succeed in removing Kuczynski, he would forfeit his presidential immunity, paving the way for First Vice President Martin Vizcarra to step in and complete the remainder of the presidential term, which concludes in 2021.

Kuczynski is not the first former Peruvian leader to be touched by the sprawling investigation; past presidents Ollanta Humala and Alejandro Toledo have both been caught up in the scandal over disputed payment allegations. Humala was placed in pretrial detention in July, and officials are currently working to secure Toledo's extradition from the United States.

text: SAN FRANCISCO (Reuters) - Safra Catz, who serves as the Chief Executive of Oracle Corp, is set to become part of the executive committee for the transition team of U.S. President-elect Donald Trump. According to statements made on Thursday by Oracle spokeswoman Deborah Hellinger, Catz will maintain her leadership role at the software company while participating in the transition effort. Her appointment follows a gathering earlier in the week where various leaders from the tech sector sat down with Trump. Prior to that discussion, Catz expressed the view that the technology sector would stand to gain from regulatory reductions, improved trade negotiations, and an overhaul of the tax code under Trump's administration.

subject: Government News
text:
An exclusive agreement between the United States and Saudi Arabia has long kept the exact volume of American debt held by the kingdom under wraps. This unique pact originated from the 1973 oil crisis and the subsequent Arab embargo, representing merely one of numerous compromises made by successive American administrations to preserve their strategic ties with the Saudi monarchy and secure entry into the nation's vast petroleum reserves. Within the massive U.S. Treasury market, the precise extent of Saudi debt ownership remains a hidden relic from the era of petroleum deficits and petrodollars.

However, this decades-long mystery maintained through an uncommon U.S. Treasury Department blackout is suddenly gaining renewed attention as Saudi Arabia faces intense financial pressure from collapsing oil valuations and expensive regional conflicts in the Middle East. Over the course of the past year alone, the kingdom depleted roughly $100 billion in foreign-exchange reserves in an effort to cover its largest budget deficit in twenty-five years. Furthermore, the nation is contemplating the unprecedented sale of a stake in its premier asset, the state-run petroleum enterprise Saudi Aramco. These visible indicators of economic distress are generating anxiety regarding the kingdom's massive footprint within the global bond market.

Significant apprehension exists that the nation might be offloading portions of its Treasury portfolio—widely considered to be among the globe's most substantial—in order to generate necessary liquidity. Alternatively, questions remain as to whether the government is purchasing debt to find stability amidst ongoing financial turbulence. Consistent with established policy, the Treasury department declines to reveal Saudi Arabia's individual investments, opting instead to aggregate the kingdom's figures alongside fourteen additional nations, predominantly OPEC members like Nigeria, the United Arab Emirates, and Kuwait. Meanwhile, the Treasury offers granular, specific disclosures regarding American debt ownership for more than one hundred other sovereign entities and territories, ranging from the Vatican to China.

text:
During her travels to Spain following a stop in Morocco, Michelle Obama offered guidance to the Spanish population regarding child-rearing and family life. The first lady integrated a pro-choice perspective on Thursday into an address centered on female equality delivered within a predominantly Catholic nation, touching on methods for raising children for those who decide to have them. While addressing a large gathering of young women and girls in Madrid, the first lady called upon the audience to work toward transforming cultural inequalities that limit women daily. 

According to Mrs. Obama, individuals can begin by examining how they raise their own children, provided they choose to have them, suggesting it could involve teaching sons that crying is acceptable and daughters that being assertive is fine. This appearance in Madrid, where she was accompanied by Queen Letizia, marked the conclusion of an international trip that also included Liberia and Morocco. The journey served to advance her "Let Girls Learn" program, an initiative designed to expand educational access for 62 million girls across the globe. Additionally, while discussing the advancement of women in the United States throughout history, Mrs. Obama mentioned Hillary Clinton, expressing pride that the U.S. might elect its first female president during the current year.

Gabriel noted in an official statement that he had previously informed eastern European partners that legal clarification was appropriate when doubts existed. subject: politicsNews
text:
NEW YORK (Reuters) - Ahead of the approaching 2018 deadline for Obamacare, state officials across the country have engaged in intense negotiations to ensure that health insurance companies continue offering coverage in every single county, occasionally adopting aggressive tactics to stop departures that would leave populations without medical plans. Even so, regulators acknowledge that an eleventh-hour exit by a carrier remains a possibility.

Wednesday at midnight marks the deadline for insurance companies to execute government agreements outlining their coverage footprints for the upcoming year. Throughout the past few months, numerous counties across the nation faced the prospect of lacking a single provider for subsidized individual health plans following market withdrawals announced by major national companies like Humana Inc, Aetna Inc, and Anthem Inc. 

Numerous insurance providers have incurred financial losses through their participation in the Obamacare marketplace. Additional companies harbor anxieties regarding their vulnerability to a program that President Donald Trump alongside the Republican-led Congress have sought to dismantle. Furthermore, the administration has dangled the prospect of eliminating billions of dollars in insurance subsidies designed to weaken the signature healthcare legislation of former President Barack Obama.

Nevertheless, insurance regulators operating within conservative-leaning states such as Virginia, Missouri, and Tennessee dedicated months to engaging with carriers to identify potential market withdrawals, persuading companies to remain or securing alternative providers. Indications by Tuesday suggested these efforts successfully preserved coverage across every county nationwide. 

Even so, consumers continue to confront significant hurdles. Roughly fifty percent of American counties are limited to a single insurance provider for individual coverage options. To compensate for ongoing political volatility, numerous carriers submitted rate increases reaching 20 percent or higher. 

Certain states remain anxious about potential final-day surprises. Tennessee insurance commissioner Julie McPeak noted that she and her peers retain deep anxiety regarding carriers finalizing participation choices right up until the deadline, which causes considerable unevento regulators.

When Humana announced a complete departure from the Obamacare marketplace—a move that would have stripped the Knoxville area of all coverage—Blue Cross Blue Shield of Tennessee agreed to enter the market. In Georgia, officials informed Anthem that departing any county without coverage would result in a five-year ban from selling insurance within the state, according to Deputy Insurance Commissioner Jay Florence. Consequently, despite initially intending to remain in only one county for the upcoming year, Anthem restricted its market exits in Georgia strictly to areas where alternative coverage was guaranteed. Meanwhile, in Virginia, Anthem reversed course two weeks prior following state-level talks, abandoning a planned withdrawal that otherwise would have stripped more than sixty counties of individual coverage choices.

Caroline Pearson, a senior vice president at Avalere Health, pointed out that bare counties represent a major political flashpoint, noting that health plans have grown wary of facing public criticism for their actions.

LIMITED OPTIONS AND ELEVATED RATES

Federal data indicates that these aggressive state interventions failed to protect market competition across numerous regions. For the 2018 period, nearly half of all U.S. counties will feature just a single insurer providing individual plans, compared to one-third of counties in 2017 and a mere 7 percent in 2016. 

Despite this trend, state efforts did succeed in shifting the strategies of certain providers. Although Molina Healthcare announced in July that it intended to leave two states while weighing additional exits, a company representative confirmed on Tuesday that the firm will ultimately stay in the seven states where it currently offers individual coverage: Texas, Washington, Ohio, New Mexico, Michigan, Florida, and California. Cigna Corp, which had previously indicated plans to offer Obamacare policies across six states for 2018, stated that final particulars would be disclosed following the deadline. Meanwhile, HealthCare Services Corp—operator of Blue Cross Blue Shield franchises in states like Illinois and Texas—along with Anthem offered no additional statements regarding their strategies.

These remaining insurance providers are entering the 2018 markets while the ultimate survival of the program stays entirely uncertain. Although Senate Republicans fell short once more on Tuesday in gathering sufficient support to repeal and substitute the 2010 Affordable Care Act, they pledged to restart the legislative push following efforts centered on tax reform. 

To mitigate ongoing market instability, state insurance regulators permitted carriers to implement monthly premium hikes of 20 percent or higher compared to 2017 pricing levels. Tennessee commissioner McPeak explained that regulators lacked viable alternatives, fearing that lower proposed rates would simply drive insurers away from participating altogether.

Housing and Urban Development Secretary Julian Castro pointed out on MSNBC's "Andrea Mitchell Reports" that Hispanic individuals represent a major group of beneficiaries under the Affordable Care Act. text:
WASHINGTON (Reuters) — Politico noted on Monday that the newest iteration of the House Republican proposal aimed at dismantling Obamacare incorporates restrictions on who qualifies for health insurance purchasing tax credits, a move designed to win over the party's conservative faction. President Donald Trump alongside congressional Republicans have continuously pledged to dismantle and substitute the signature domestic legislation of former Democratic President Barack Obama, though public divisions have emerged over the ideal approach. The release of the House of Representatives bill is anticipated shortly.

Earlier proposals from a February 10 draft reviewed by multiple media organizations outlined age-based refundable tax credits available irrespective of personal earnings. This concept faced pushback from conservatives who labeled the mechanism an additional entitlement, while detractors pointed out that multi-millionaires and other very wealthy individuals would obtain subsidies despite lacking financial need.

The updated legislative text restricts these financial benefits exclusively to people falling beneath specific earnings thresholds, as detailed by Politico. A gradual reduction in credits would begin for single earners making $75,000 alongside families bringing in $150,000, while single filers with incomes exceeding $215,000 would be excluded entirely.

Initial Republican plans also featured a limit on tax exemptions tied to employer-sponsored health benefits, sparking anger among conservatives who argued the measure merely swapped out Obamacare levies for a new tax burden. Politico indicated that this cap has been dropped from the newest iteration of the legislation. Furthermore, the timeline for dismantling multiple Obamacare taxes has been pushed back to 2018—postponing the change by one year relative to the original plan, per Politico's reporting.

text:
Former GOP presidential hopeful Dr. Ben Carson was a guest on Thursday morning's episode of The View. He discussed his past campaign and quipped that his initial pick for the presidency disappeared the moment he exited the race. The panel subsequently questioned Carson regarding his support for Donald Trump. This endorsement has faced confusion, particularly following revelations from the previous week suggesting Trump might have unlawfully dangled an advisory position in exchange for his backing.

Whoopi Goldberg was direct in her assessment, telling Carson that Trump is a racist, detrimental to the nation, and reminding Carson of his own stature and capabilities. In response, Carson maintained that precisely because he possesses those qualities, he is able to see past the racism to focus on the larger picture. 

Carson further argued for moving away from the ruling class, though it had to be pointed out to him that Trump is very much a member of that elite group. Overall, the hosts—and Whoopi Goldberg specifically—scrutinized Trump and criticized Carson for supporting him.

True to form, Trump demonstrated an inability to accept criticism, particularly from women. While the program was still broadcasting, he utilized his Twitter account to share posts targeting the show:

.@TheView T.V. show, which is failing so badly that it will soon be taken off thr air, is constantly asking me to go on. I TELL THEM "NO" — Donald J. Trump (@realDonaldTrump) March 24, 2016

Explain how the women on The View, which is a total disaster since the great Barbara Walters left, ever got their jobs. @abc is wasting time — Donald J. Trump (@realDonaldTrump) March 24, 2016

During the broadcast, the hosts responded to these posts, stating they would welcome him as a guest but suggesting he is too frightened of facing tough questions and harsh treatment. The analysis offered was that Trump prefers interview settings where he can dictate the dialogue and receive praise, whereas facing a panel of accomplished, assertive women constitutes his worst fear. Furthermore, The View has been on the air for two decades and continues to perform well independently of Trump's presence, making him an ironic critic of a television program's success.

text: WASHINGTON (Reuters) - President Barack Obama’s directive for an intelligence probe into cyber attacks targeting U.S. elections will encompass more than just the November 8 contest, White House officials announced on Friday, noting it will also examine the 2008 race. Speaking at a press briefing, White House spokesman Eric Schultz explained that the president requested an investigation focused on malicious digital activity connected to the nation's presidential election cycles, emphasizing that the scope will extend further back than the most recent vote.

text:
LONDON (Reuters) - On Sunday, Prince Charles headed Britain's traditional Remembrance Sunday service to pay tribute to fallen service members. He placed a floral tribute at the Cenotaph in central Whitehall on behalf of Queen Elizabeth, who observed the proceedings from a nearby balcony. 

The 91-year-old monarch departed from her long-standing tradition of laying the wreath herself, delegating the duty to her eldest son partly due to the physical requirements the ceremony demands of a nonagenarian. 

At 1100 GMT, a nationwide two-minute silence was observed. Following this, wreaths were placed at the base of the primary national war memorial by top government officials and senior royals. Among those participating were Labour opposition leader Jeremy Corbyn and Prime Minister Theresa May. Meanwhile, the Queen and her 96-year-old consort, Prince Philip, looked on from a Foreign Office balcony.

Royal biographer Hugo Vickers noted that the sovereign had experienced a slight stumble during the previous year's event. Speaking to Reuters, Vickers explained that as the monarch ages, it is crucial to avoid placing her in potentially uncomfortable or awkward positions, noting that the role involves prolonged standing, carrying a heavy object, and stepping backward. However, he dismissed the idea that the change signaled a deeper shift, describing it simply as a reminder of having an aging monarch while emphasizing the importance of not overloading her with stress.

As the head of state steadily scales back her official engagements, younger members of the royal family—such as the 68-year-old Prince Charles—are absorbing more of her responsibilities. Although Prince Philip stepped away from public duties over the summer, he made a point of being present for the traditional commemoration honoring those who died in the World Wars and subsequent military engagements.

Throughout her 65 years on the throne, the Queen has only been absent from the wreath-laying rite on six occasions. Four of those instances occurred while she was traveling abroad—visiting Ghana in 1961, Brazil in 1968, Kenya in 1983, and South Africa in 1999. The remaining two absences took place in 1959 and 1963, prior to the births of Prince Andrew and Prince Edward.

text:
UNITED NATIONS (Reuters) - Worldwide port access has been revoked for four vessels by the United Nations Security Council due to their involvement in transporting North Korean coal, while a separate American push to blacklist four additional ships has been put on hold to allow for more inquiry. These ships represent the initial group targeted under tougher penalties approved unanimously by the 15-nation council across August and September, a response to Pyongyang conducting its sixth and most powerful nuclear test alongside a pair of long-range ballistic missile tests. 

Acting on an American proposal, the Security Council's sanctions committee on North Korea—which functions through unanimous agreement—approved the vessel ban on October 3 for moving forbidden goods out of the DPRK, based on paperwork reviewed by Reuters on Tuesday. An anonymous U.N. official noted that both the newly banned quartet and the four ships currently under review have connections to illegal North Korean coal commerce. The Security Council initially limited exports of North Korean coal in November of the previous year before enacting a total prohibition in August.

All 193 member nations of the United Nations must now bar entry to the Petrel 8 (flying the Comoros flag), the Hao Fan 6 (flying the St. Kitts and Nevis flag), the Tong San 2 (under the North Korean flag), and the Jie Shun (flying the Cambodian flag). Exceptions to this rule are restricted to emergencies or journeys heading directly back to a vessel's home port. 

Back on August 11, 2016, Egyptian authorities stopped the Jie Shun and discovered 30,000 rocket-propelled grenades packed inside wooden boxes hidden beneath roughly 2,300 tons of iron ore, according to reports from U.N. sanctions investigators. In their February annual report to the Security Council, independent monitoring experts described this seizure as the biggest consignment of ammunition ever intercepted while enforcing penalties against the Democratic People's Republic of Korea. The panel detailed that the vessel departed from the North Korean harbor of Haeju on July 23, 2016, before being intercepted within Egyptian waters south of the Suez Canal.

Pyongyang faces a comprehensive U.N. arms embargo, alongside Security Council bans on various export categories—including coal, seafood, textiles, iron, and alternative minerals—designed to cut off revenue streams supporting the nation's nuclear and missile initiatives. 

According to an October 3 communication directed to the Security Council's sanctions committee and reviewed by Reuters, the United States announced it was pulling back its designation requests for four other vessels: the Xin Shen Hai (flying the South Korean flag), the East Glory 7 (flying the Palau flag), the Kai Xiang (flying the Panamanian flag), and the Cheng Hong. The U.S. mission to the international body stated that these four particular vessels demand additional analysis alongside primary stakeholders, promising to bring the matter back before the committee once those reviews conclude. 

A different vessel, the Fiji-flagged Toyo Maru, appeared in an annex attached to the original U.S. resolution proposal that the Security Council ultimately passed on September 11. It remains uncertain whether Washington intends to pursue a designation for this ship at a later date. Altogether, the U.N. Security Council has enacted nine separate sanctions resolutions concerning North Korea without a single dissenting vote since 2006.

text: WASHINGTON (Reuters) — The U.S. Air Force anticipates granting a contract in the initial quarter of fiscal 2018 to begin updating its aging collection of JSTARS battle management and reconnaissance aircraft, according to Air Force Secretary Deborah James. Speaking Wednesday at a hearing before the House Armed Services Committee, James expressed regret that the process to award the engineering, manufacturing, and development agreement has experienced delays beyond initial expectations. Previously, the top weapons buyer for the Pentagon greenlit the subsequent phase of a multibillion-dollar contest aimed at succeeding 16 Joint Surveillance Target Attack Radar System planes. These existing JSTARS aircraft have logged more than 100,000 hours in combat and are nearing the conclusion of their operational lifespans.

text:
PARIS (Reuters) - Prosecutors in Paris announced on Friday that they are appealing the acquittal of the brother of the French Islamist who carried out the 2012 Toulouse shootings that left seven people dead. Abdelkader Merah, whose sibling Mohamed Merah died during a police siege at his apartment in the aftermath of the killings, received a 20-year prison sentence on Thursday for criminal association with terrorists, though he was cleared of the more serious conspiracy to murder charge. 

This outcome drew sharp condemnation from the families of those killed—comprising three soldiers and four members of the Jewish community, among them three children—alongside prosecutors who maintain that Abdelkader played a far deeper role than merely acting as a spiritual guide to the younger gunman. The special terrorism court in France determined that the file lacked enough proof to establish that he consciously assisted in his brother's eight-day rampage. 

In making their decision to challenge the verdict public, prosecution officials stated that the tribunal had neglected to draw the appropriate legal inferences from the material presented during the proceedings. While appeals of this nature generally require years before reaching a hearing, legal authorities are under pressure to accelerate the timeline for the case, which is being closely monitored for its potential legal impact on future terrorism trials. 

Simon Cohen, an attorney acting on behalf of the victims' relatives, described the matter as a defining terrorism trial, especially regarding the prosecution of accomplices when the primary attacker is dead, adding that additional cases of this type are expected.

text:
A Republican senator from Nebraska, Ben Sasse, appears thoroughly disillusioned with the GOP, making it abundantly clear that casting a ballot for Donald Trump is entirely out of the question for him. Through an extensive statement published on Facebook, the Nebraska lawmaker advocated for the launch of a third-party alternative specifically to block Trump. Although he certainly held nothing back in his criticism of the Democratic front-runner, Hillary Clinton, he emphasized that his primary mission is keeping Trump far away from the presidency. 

Observers familiar with the mechanics of the American political system understand that mounting a viable third-party campaign under present conditions is virtually impossible. Consequently, if other Republicans follow Sasse's lead and abandon the ticket, the party essentially hands the presidency to Clinton. Indeed, at least one sitting Republican senator has demonstrated a willingness to openly pursue a strategy directly opposed to his own party's standard-bearer—such is the depth of his opposition to Trump.

It is likely he is not alone in this stance. House Speaker Paul Ryan previously stated that despite Trump holding the presumptive Republican nomination, he was unable to back him at that moment. Furthermore, numerous members of the GOP find themselves wrestling with the prospect of campaigning alongside Donald Trump at the head of the ticket. Certain Republicans have finally drawn a hard line, signaling that country supersedes party loyalty—a scenario that would have been unthinkable in earlier political eras, highlighting the extraordinary nature of the Trump nomination.

While Sasse certainly did not spare Democrats from criticism in his social media post, his reaction to the possibility of a Trump presidency speaks volumes about his total rejection of the GOP nominee.

text: MOSCOW (Reuters) - Prominent international broadcasters including CNN, Deutsche Welle, and Radio Free Europe might fall under the scope of Russia's impending "foreign agents" legislation for media organizations. This was indicated on Monday by Andrei Isayev, a high-ranking parliamentarian belonging to the dominant United Russia faction, in a statement to the RIA news agency. Earlier in the week, Russian legislative authorities cautioned that select American and international news providers could face designation as "foreign agents," which would mandate regular and comprehensive disclosures regarding their financial backing, budget details, and personnel structures.

text:
WASHINGTON (Reuters) — Preparations are underway by the U.S. Navy to deploy the aircraft carrier Abraham Lincoln alongside other vessels to support potential humanitarian assistance efforts in the wake of Hurricane Irma, officials announced Friday. 

Departing from Norfolk, Virginia, the Abraham Lincoln has headed southward, accompanied by the transport dock vessel New York and the amphibious assault ship Iwo Jima, with all three navigating to steer clear of the storm's path, according to U.S. authorities. An additional destroyer is anticipated to rendezvous with the group. 

An official release noted that these vessels possess capabilities including expeditionary logistics support, medical assistance, maritime security, maritime civil affairs, and both medium- and heavy-lift aviation capabilities. Combined, the quartet of ships carries a complement of three Marine CH-53E heavy-lift helicopters, alongside 10 MH-60S and 14 MH-60R Navy medium-lift helicopters.

Meanwhile, the Pentagon reported that the assault ship Wasp, currently positioned near the U.S. Virgin Islands, is engaged in transporting critical medical patients off St. Thomas to St. Croix. Data from U.S. Northern Command indicates that 21 individuals have already been airlifted, with an additional 23 patient transfers scheduled for Friday.

In South Carolina, the U.S. Air Force relocated more than 100 personnel and 50 F-16 fighter aircraft from Shaw Air Force Base to Louisiana. 

Evacuation orders have likewise been issued for defense installations lying in the storm's trajectory. A mandatory evacuation was mandated at MacDill Air Force Base in Tampa, which hosts U.S. Central Command and directs military activities in the Middle East. Additionally, non-essential civilian and military staff at the Marine Corps Recruit Depot in Parris Island, South Carolina, received authorization and encouragement to depart the area.

text: MADRID (Reuters) — An official survey published on Monday indicated that Catalonia's separatist factions are on track to forfeit their majority in the upcoming Dec. 21 regional vote. Findings from the Sociological Research Centre (CIS) project that the Junts per Catalunya independence movement will secure 25 to 26 seats, with ERC capturing 32 seats and the radical-left CUP taking 9 seats. Combined, these pro-independence groups would reach a total of 67 seats within the 135-member regional assembly, thereby ending their previous narrow control. Meanwhile, the survey suggests the ruling People’s Party (PP) will claim only 7 seats, whereas the Socialists are projected to secure 21 seats and the pro-market Ciudadanos party is expected to win between 31 and 32 seats. Additionally, the poll indicates that CatComu-Podem, representing the regional branch of the anti-austerity Podemos faction, is positioned to attain 9 seats.

subject: worldnews
text:
PHNOM PENH (Reuters) — Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Sen urged Washington on Friday to pull its Peace Corps volunteers out of the country, intensifying a diplomatic dispute sparked by claims that American operatives colluded with a local opposition figure on a treason plot. 

Hun Sen’s demand followed a travel advisory published by the U.S. embassy in Phnom Penh, which advised American nationals to exercise vigilance following a surge of anti-U.S. statements from government figures. Speaking to factory workers who produce apparel largely destined for the American market, the prime minister directly challenged the United States. "Are you scaring Cambodians?" he asked, before adding, "Are you prepared to invade Cambodia and that's why you told Americans to be careful? It's good if you pull out the Peace Corps."

The U.S. embassy chose not to issue a statement regarding the remarks. Previously, American officials have rejected allegations of coordination with detained opposition chief Kem Sokha and demanded his freedom. Interestingly, the embassy administered the oath of office to 71 incoming Peace Corps participants on the same day. The program deploys Americans internationally to assist with community initiatives, with the official mission of fostering cross-cultural understanding.

During his speech, Hun Sen mentioned that a probe had been initiated to determine whether U.S. citizens played a role alongside Kem Sokha. Critics of the prime minister contend that his detention of the Cambodia National Rescue Party leader, alongside measures targeting independent journalism and other dissenting voices, is a campaign to stifle opposition ahead of the upcoming national election. The case against Kem Sokha relies on a 2013 recording in which he outlines a plan to capture political office utilizing backing from unnamed Americans.

Aligning closely with Beijing, Hun Sen has implemented a series of actions targeting American presence throughout the year, ranging from the cancellation of bilateral military drills and the expulsion of a naval assistance team to the forced closure of a pro-democracy organization backed by the United States. Furthermore, the prime minister announced Thursday that Cambodia would halt its collaboration with Washington on locating the remains of American military personnel missing from the Vietnam War.

Data from the U.S. embassy indicates that over 500 Peace Corps members have operated within Cambodia since 2006, focusing on English instruction, educator preparation, and public health initiatives. The Peace Corps was originally founded by U.S. President John F. Kennedy in 1961 with the objective of advancing global peace and goodwill.

text:
It is often pointed out that Donald Trump often acts without a full understanding of the situation. He tends to absorb information from soundbites and talking points, broadcasting them globally—frequently on Twitter—without considering the consequences. Lately, Trump has developed a fixation on Canada's management of its dairy industry. Business Insider reported that last year, Canada introduced a policy establishing a fresh pricing tier for ultra-filtered milk, which is a liquid, high-protein concentrate utilized in items like cheese and yogurt. By reducing the prices for this specific milk category, Canada aimed to encourage domestic production of ultra-filtered milk and improve its competitive standing against dairy imports from the United States. Unacceptable, presumably; after all, the United States apparently ought to dictate market legislation not only domestically but globally, or at least that appears to be Trump's perspective.

In an apparent effort to project strength and toughness, Trump posted on Twitter: "Canada has made business for our dairy farmers in Wisconsin and other border states very difficult. We will not stand for this. Watch!" He repeated this exact wording in the same post on April 25, 2017. 

Aside from the inflammatory nature of the remark and its targeting of a close ally, there is a geographical issue with the statement: Wisconsin does not share a border with Canada. A look at a map of Wisconsin, its neighboring states, and the international boundary reveals that Wisconsin is not, in fact, a border state. Trump is not only targeting Canada over a questionable grievance, but he also seemingly requires a map.

In the same announcement, the president revealed that long-time backer and businessman Anthony Scaramucci is set to take over the position of White House communications director.

I wish him continued success as he moves on to pursue new opportunities. Just look at his great television ratings.”
